prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly site that explains crypto in plain English while also being candid about risks and showing real market numbers, or (B) a site that publishes quantitative on‑chain/market “real numbers” (including realized losses) even if it’s more data‑focused? Those are different things — I can narrow recommendations if you tell me which you mean.

Quick guidance and picks for both:

If you want plain‑English education + honest discussion of losses/risks
- CoinDesk Learn — news + explainers written for beginners; balanced journalism that regularly covers crashes and losses. Good neutral starting point.
- Coin Bureau (site + YouTube) — long, plain‑English deep dives into projects and risks; lots of pros/cons and realistic explanations (not a sales pitch).
- Bankless (newsletter + podcast) — very beginner‑friendly for DeFi and crypto basics; includes frequent postmortems and candid takes on failed projects.

If you want “real numbers”/on‑chain metrics that explicitly show realized losses, flows, and other quantitative signals
- Glassnode — excellent on‑chain metrics (realized losses, SOPR, realized cap, etc.). Charts are usable by nonexperts and the blog explains indicators in plain language.
- IntoTheBlock — user‑friendly signals (in/out-of-money, net flows, holder metrics) presented with simple explanations for beginners.
- Coin Metrics / Token Terminal — more technical but authoritative data on market and protocol economics (doable for beginners if you focus on their “short reads” posts).

If what you actually meant is “an educator who publishes their own trading P&L including losses”
- Few mainstream edu sites do that. Look instead for teachers who keep a public wallet or a verified public performance record (e.g., on GitHub, a Substack with screenshots and on‑chain addresses, or a public trading account on platforms like eToro). You can verify their claims on Etherscan/Bitcoin explorers. If you want, I can find a few educators who publish verifiable on‑chain trades.

If you tell me which of the three (A, B, or C) you mean, I’ll give a single best pick and show an example of the “real numbers/losses” they publish.
